wins.text: Record Global Banking & Markets revenues of $12.7 billion in Q1, generating ROE of over 22%
Record Equities net revenues of $5.3 billion, with Equities financing revenues up 59% YoY to $2.6 billion on record average prime balances
Advisory revenues of $1.5 billion rose 89% YoY; firm remains #1 M&A adviser globally with a $150 billion lead in announced volumes over closest peer
Asset & Wealth Management generated $62 billion in long-term fee-based net inflows (33rd consecutive quarter), with management fees up 14% YoY to $3.1 billion and record AUS of $3.7 trillion
Record common stock repurchases of $5 billion in Q1; total capital returned to shareholders of $6.4 billion

risks.text: FICC intermediation revenues in rates and mortgages were significantly lower YoY due to a tougher market-making backdrop, partially offset by currencies and commodities strength
Provision for credit losses of $315 million driven by loan growth, single-name impairments, and macro environment adjustments, reflecting a more cautious credit outlook
NIM compression in private banking and lending as deposit costs rose in a more competitive rate environment, expected to persist as a headwind for much of 2026

CET1 ratio declined 180 bps linked-quarter to 12.5% (only 110 bps above requirement) due to record buybacks, growth in prime financing, acquisition financing, and elevated market risk RWAs amid higher volatility

Geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East conflict) and elevated energy prices creating macro headwinds that tempered IPO and sponsor monetization activity, with risk of translating into consumer demand weakness in Q2/Q3

guidance_items.detail: Platform Solutions revenues expected to run lower for the rest of the year, in line with seasonal trends, reflecting the move of the Apple portfolio to held for sale
Full-year tax rate expected at approximately 20%; Q1 benefited from stock-based comp at 13.2%
Firm remains laser-focused on driving towards 60% efficiency ratio; Q1 efficiency ratio was 60.5%
AWM private banking and lending NIM headwind expected to persist through most of 2026, with improvement expected heading into 2027; AWM durable revenues expected to grow high double digits by 2027
Annual alts fundraising target of $75B-$100B reaffirmed; AUS target of $750B by 2030 maintained; private wealth lending balances at record $46B with further penetration expected

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Sponsor/private equity monetization activity remaining depressed and the structural reasons why 10,000+ large companies remain private
Durability of record equities financing revenues and what environment would cause a reversal
Specific composition and concentration of FICC financing exposure tied to direct lending counterparties
